evals.prompt: Write the hero copy for our landing page. Product is Ledgerline, a bookkeeping tool for freelance designers. Traffic is a cold Instagram ad. We have 4,200 paying users and it connects to Stripe and Xero.
evals.expected_output: A brief with inferred fields marked, then Options A, B, and C, each with headline, subhead, and CTA, and a one-sentence recommendation
assertions: Brief names the awareness stage as unaware or problem-aware
At least one option opens with the reader's problem rather than the product name
The supplied specifics (4,200, Stripe, Xero) appear in at least one option and none are replaced by 'thousands' or 'your favourite tools'
No headline reuses the phrase 'bookkeeping tool for freelance designers' verbatim
No banned word and no em dash, double hyphen, or spaced hyphen in any option
Exactly three options for a hero, each structurally different

evals.prompt: Our pricing page button says 'Get started'. Improve the CTA.
evals.expected_output: Two labelled options for a single string, one recommended, with a one-line reason
assertions: Exactly two options, not three
Each option names the outcome or destination (e.g. trial length, 'See plans'), not a bare 'Get started' or 'Learn more'
Each label is 2 to 5 words
The response does not expand into a full page audit

evals.prompt: Write the error message for when a CSV import fails because the file has more than 10,000 rows. Also give me the button label for the dialog that deletes an imported dataset.
evals.expected_output: One error string stating what happened, why, and the recovery, plus a verb-plus-object destructive label with Cancel as the safe action
assertions: Error message names the 10,000-row limit and a recovery action (split the file, remove rows)
Error message avoids 'invalid', 'illegal', 'Something went wrong', and raw exception text
Error message is 18 words or fewer
Destructive button is Verb plus Noun naming the object (e.g. 'Delete dataset'), not 'Confirm', 'OK', 'Yes', or bare 'Delete'
No persuasion framework or marketing framing is applied to the state copy

evals.prompt: Remove the AI-isms from this: 'In today's fast-paced landscape, Relay seamlessly integrates with your favourite tools, ensuring your team stays aligned. It's not just a deployment tool - it's a paradigm shift. Whether you're a solo founder or an enterprise, Relay empowers you to ship with confidence.'
evals.expected_output: A before/after diff with [AI-ISM] flags naming the pattern type, and a rewrite that carries the facts without the tells
assertions: Flags include a Tier 1 word (seamlessly, landscape, or paradigm), the participle tail 'ensuring...', the negative parallelism 'not just X, it's Y', the false-breadth 'Whether you're X or Y', and the spaced hyphen standing in for an em dash
The rewrite does not replace a flagged word with a table neighbour (no 'leverage', 'harness', 'robust', 'streamline', 'elevate')
The rewrite names a specific integration or asks for one via a [PLACEHOLDER] rather than keeping 'your favourite tools'
Output follows the Copy Audit before/after template with a Summary block

evals.prompt: Fix the copy in this hero. The repo's VOICE.md says: 'Signature words: unlock. Locale: en-AU.' Hero copy: 'Unlock your team's best work. Organise every project, colour-code priorities, and ship on time. Trusted by thousands of teams. Get started.'
evals.expected_output: A point-edit or restoration pass that keeps 'unlock', keeps en-AU spelling, and flags only the 3 to 7 weakest lines
assertions: 'unlock' is not flagged as a banned word or [AI-ISM]
No en-AU spelling is changed to en-US
Between 3 and 7 flags total
Every fact, number, and link in the Before appears in the After
